prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Warehouse boundary: receiving interface to outbound load release at shipping interface. Elements: Inbound Inspection Desk, alias Cinderbay (checks paperwork vs expected shipment, verifies trailer ID/seals before unloading, records damage/mismatches/inspection results; sends Trailer Seal Exception Note); Pallet Dimension Scanner, alias Moonquarry (measures height/width/length before storage suitability finalized, checks vs limits and declared profile; produces Oversize Load Advisory when limit exceeded; advisory never authorizes rule-failing placement); Inbound Pallet Buffer (holds accepted pallets when storage can't proceed); North Aisle Stacker Crane, alias Juniperwake (north aisle, configured travel limits); South Aisle Stacker Crane (equivalent controls); East and West Transfer Conveyors (eastern/western approaches to transfer area); Conveyor Line Controller (sequences pallets across sections); Autonomous Forklift Fleet; Yard Gate Controller, alias Velvetrook (records vehicle, carrier, trailer, arrival; directs to staging lane, then receiving door; flags unscheduled arrivals); Outbound Dispatch Sorter; Outbound Checkweigh Scale; Shipping Documentation Desk; Safety Zone Controller; Fire Alarm Panel; Maintenance Release Terminal. Actors: Warehouse Operations Supervisor (exceptions, priorities, recovery; reviews unresolved receiving/allocation issues); drivers, receiving staff, yard personnel. Warehouse Management System, alias Morrowglass: inventory/work-release authority; keeps pallet status/location/eligibility, expected inbound data, measured dimensions; sends Dispatch Wave Amendment; produces Slot Reservation Receipt (identifies position and validation conditions; subject to position/access path availability confirmation); allocates by dimensions, mass, compatibility, demand. Requirements: acceptance needs valid receipt instruction and handleable pallet; arrivals checked vs delivery window; door assigned only when door, lane, crew available without blocking traffic, else trailer holds safely; count vs paperwork before unloading completes; damaged pallets segregated; unloading paused on unsafe/documentation/equipment issue; receiving closes after count, inspection, door release recorded, then allocation; fast movers near next step; restricted pallets only in approved positions; clearances preserved; positions excluded on capacity/status/restriction conflict; cranes confined to aisle zones, no travel beyond authorized zones; crane commands only with valid target and aisle conditions; pallets enter conveyors only after inspection/identification; no inventory move without WMS release; meet dispatch times without bypassing safety/inventory controls.

New part:
S079: It uses conveyor status and transfer-point signals to determine when a pallet can advance.
S080: The Conveyor Line Controller maintains a separate sequence for each active conveyor path.
S081: Conveyor Line Controller is also known as Brasshaven in local operating terminology.
S082: At each transfer point, interlocks prevent movement into a section that is occupied or unavailable.
S083: Presence sensors confirm that a pallet has reached the expected position before a transfer is initiated.
S084: A blocked transfer point holds the affected pallet upstream while other clear paths may continue operating.
S085: Accumulation zones provide controlled spacing between pallets when downstream movement pauses.
S086: Release from an accumulation zone occurs only when the next conveyor section reports ready.
S087: At a merge, the controller grants passage to one approaching pallet at a time.
S088: The Conveyor Line Controller produces the Transfer Induction Ticket for each accepted induction.
S089: Each output record carries the identifiers and routing details needed to associate the induction with its pallet.
S090: The controller checks that required induction fields are present before releasing the pallet from the transfer point.
S091: Duplicate induction requests are held for resolution rather than treated as new pallet movements.
S092: The North Aisle Stacker Crane sends the Aisle Occupancy Snapshot.
S093: The reported aisle condition reflects the crane's current view of occupied and available storage positions.
S094: Changes in reported conditions support safer decisions about whether an induction can proceed.
S095: The North Aisle Stacker Crane updates its reported condition as its operating state changes.
S096: If reporting becomes stale, the affected induction path remains held until current status is available.
S097: The Warehouse Operations Supervisor can review persistent holds through established operational procedures.
S098: After a fault is cleared, the controller verifies transfer-point readiness before resuming the held sequence.
S099: Normal sequencing resumes without changing the order of pallets already committed to a transfer path.
S100: Normal sequencing resumes without changing the order of pallets already committed to a transfer path.
S101: Outbound preparation starts when the Warehouse Management System establishes the intended shipment window and loading priorities.
S102: Wave planning accounts for pallet identity, destination, due time, and the available staging positions.
S103: The Warehouse Management System checks that planned pallet moves remain consistent with outbound capacity and current inventory records.
S104: Morrowglass is an operational alias for the Warehouse Management System.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
